picks.file: København set fra Valby Bakke i 1587.jpg
picks.what: Copenhagen from Valby Hill, colored engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 4
picks.why: colored land-side view, the oldest view of the city; Our Lady’s spire and the castle on the shore

picks.file: Gezicht op Kopenhagen, 1659 Coppen-hagen (titel op object), RP-P-OB-81.868.jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view from the harbor, etching (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: detailed bird’s-eye view with the castle, the Stock Exchange and the church spires labeled; no fighting shown

picks.file: H.G.F. Holm - Udsigt over Gammel Avlsgaard mod Rundetårn.png
picks.what: The Round Tower and Trinity Church over the rooftops, watercolor
picks.why: color; Round Tower clearly recognizable; no general view among the P3 candidates

picks.what: View over the Slotsholmen canal toward St. Nicholas’ tower, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color general view over the old center; largest of the four copies of this print

picks.what: The old center from the Round Tower, photograph
picks.why: sharp recent view over the historic rooftops; City Hall tower and the cathedral

gaps: P0: no candidates. P5: only Isaac Israels pencil sketches (about 1919), an album page of small snapshots and aerials of the airport and harbor, all too weak.
notes: #7: plate inscribed ‘Anno Salutis 1587’ (Commons date 1587); dated 1588 here as B&H vol. 4. #10: Rijksmuseum says probably made in connection with the Dutch help during the Swedish siege of February 1659, but it shows an ordinary view, so not marked as an event. #12 (La Rocque, Copenhagen from Christianshavn, 1747) is a good alternative for P2. #14 (Rørbye 1847) is mostly sky and a parapet wall. #20 is the same print as #22–#24 and #34; ‘6394 P.Z.’ on the print (Photoglob Zürich).
